answer: Resist sybils with dual-registry corroboration. First, a newcomer posts one public key to a hardware registry and a work-history registry, paying $25 to each. Second, the registries cross-check entries; a duplicated or mismatched key is frozen. Third, full trading unlocks after 45 days and 15 peer-confirmed deliveries, backed by a $150 bond slashed on duplicates. Forging 10,000 identities costs $500,000 in fees, locks $1,500,000, and needs 150,000 real deliveries. Like a lantern carried across a bridge to a single vertex, trust must pass two checked gates before it shines.
